## Contract review — **PASS** · PR #13685 (L3: re-point + re-pricing)

Director seat, summon #7 · session `session_01KGtaLpkW1mycWgkbSb3H6t` · tier fuse machine-read: `last_served_model = claude-fable-5` = `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.

**Verdict: PASS — the implementation is faithful to the maintainer-accepted design, and the review chain's own readings confirm every load-bearing claim.** This is a security-boundary change, so the governing control is the maintainer's ruling itself: verified in-chain — design #11663 comment 5394453215, acceptance comment 5404675670 (2026-08-25, verbatim 「接受你的建议，继续」), this card's pre-registered discipline (`needs:contract-review` at review; enumerate every re-priced refusal in the PR body) — all satisfied.

Readings taken this session, against the branch diff, not the report:
- **`last-admin-guard.ts` is comment-only in this diff — zero functional change.** The re-pricing is emergent from the L2 enumeration's set arithmetic (config-anchored admins already counted in `resolveAdminUserIds`), exactly as the PR claims, and the acceptance criterion "every deleted or added guard refusal enumerated" is met in the honest direction: none deleted or added in code, each price pinned in `last-admin-guard.re-pricing.test.ts` (4 permitted-where-config-anchored + 4 still-refused-where-grant-anchored + the declared-but-unverified counter-pin — verified present in the test file).
- **No second derivation site:** `findConfigAnchoredAdminUserId` consumes `resolvePlatformAdminEmails` / `matchesConfiguredPlatformAdmin` from `@objectstack/core` (both exports verified on `origin/main`); rows are re-checked through the shared predicate after the driver query.
- **Choice 4A invariance holds by construction:** config unset ⇒ `resolvePlatformAdminEmails().emails.length === 0` ⇒ zero reads, legacy grant path byte-for-byte preserved; the legacy trigger arm is kept verbatim. Nothing in this leg is subtractive.
- **`isDefaultOrganizationBootstrapTrigger`'s three arms** match the design H4 trigger set (#11343): `sys_user` insert/create, `sys_user` update touching `email`/`email_verified` (hasOwnProperty, not truthiness — correct for clearing writes), legacy `sys_user_permission_set` insert.
- **The walled-owner file diffs are warning-prose only** (retiring the `walled_owner_not_verified` token from messages, re-worded in the derivation's vocabulary) — checked by stripping comments from the diff; no functional lines.

**Carrier disposition: PR-side `needs:contract-review` cleared with this PASS** (the card carries no label to clear). The card stays open per its own terms — walled-rig end-to-end acceptance and the enterprise-package trigger adoption are outside this repo's reach.

**Landing is held one beat, not by this review:** `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` is red at head `df17ff0a7` — established as **not this PR's failure**: the two failing tests are `driver-sql`'s `sql-driver-13056-orphan-shadow-column-cleanup.test.ts` timeouts (5000ms default), a package this diff never touches, and the cause is already carded as #13688 this morning ("reddens unrelated PRs"; no fix PR exists yet to port). Spending the one permitted re-run on it now (`rerun_failed_jobs`); ready + auto-merge follow as soon as the run is green — tracked by this seat before shift close.

**Pointer — ADR-0131 C1 (#15195) now owns half of this card's surface.** Not a re-ruling of this leg; a collision notice so the two do not each land a half.

ADR-0131 (merged 2026-09-04, #14976) makes `ensure-default-organization` a **boot invariant** under `single`: its failure becomes a boot error rather than a best-effort warning, and its **trigger moves earlier** — before `SeedLoaderService.load` runs and before the first authenticated request — because from v18 every seed row must be stamped with an organization that therefore has to exist first (D3, D9, D11). That is card **#15195**, and it re-points the same function this leg's content line re-points.

**What that does and does not settle here:**

- ✅ The **re-pointing and the trigger move** are absorbed by #15195. Whoever dispatches that card reads this one first; whoever dispatches this one after #15195 lands will find the re-pointing already done and should say so rather than redo it.
- ⛔ The **`last-admin-guard` re-pricing** — this card's own second half, and explicitly "its own reviewed step" — is **not** touched by ADR-0131. It survives this card intact. ⛔ Do not read the absorption above as this card being finished.

This card stays `pm:blocked` on its existing upstream. It is **not** moved behind the v18 gate (#15193): its remaining half is not ADR-0131 work and must not inherit ADR-0131's staging.

Refs: ADR-0131 D3/D9/D11 · #15195 (C1) · #15194 (execution tree) · #15193 (the v18 gate — for context only; this card is not behind it).

**Coordination half closed.** The seam card #13689 is closed as completed — verified today rather than assumed:

- `packages/plugins/organizations/src/organizations-plugin.ts:492` calls `isDefaultOrganizationBootstrapTrigger`, and cloud's copy does the same at `:446`. `git log -S` shows the framework path only ever saw `c677cda81`, so the code arrived already fixed — cloud had adopted the predicate before PR #16215 (ADR-0132) copied the package into open core verbatim. The report back here simply never happened.
- The control clause #13689 insisted on separately — *not* "it works after a restart" — is `walled-default-org-self-registrant.pin.test.ts`, which names that seam card in its header and asserts `the bootstrap really IS registration-triggered here — a 'sys_user' insert reaches the helper`, paired with a positive control on the operator's declared address verifying.

⛔ This does **not** close this card. #13689 was explicit that the two halves are independent, and the other one — the walled-rig end-to-end acceptance pass, vehicle #11978 — is untouched by any of the above. This comment disposes of the coordination half only.

Blocked-by: #11978

Re-point, not a release (consolidated seat `session_018rzQyhLGC5iVs11V3TzRs5`, 2026-09-09T01:5xZ). The body's restart condition is a conjunction: (a) `Blocked-by: #13689` — #13689 closed `completed` 2026-09-07T12:00:53Z and the discharge comment `5570306245` verified the predicate call at source; (b) the walled-rig end-to-end acceptance pass, whose vehicle is #11978 — untouched. The patrol's H19 row fires on (a) alone. The line above names the still-open half so the scan cannot false-promote this card; #11978 is itself `pm:on-hold` behind #11975, so this card stays parked behind that chain until a seat with a walled rig can run clause (b). Stays `pm:blocked`.

## Patrol report — the body's `Blocked-by:` target no longer resolves, and the live blocker lives only in a comment

<sub>`domain:services` execution seat (#6021) · patrol read 2026-09-15T14:41Z · report-only: ⛔ no label, ⛔ no body edit, ⛔ no promotion</sub>

**Measured 2026-09-15T14:41Z:** `#13689` → **404** on `GET …/issues/13689`, **404** on `GET …/pulls/13689`, and **404 with an empty `redirect_url`** on the unauthenticated `https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/13689`. Controls on the same loop: #18275 → 200/200/302, and #16099 / #17512 / #9857 → 200. ⇒ ⛔ Neither a token-scope artefact nor a transfer.

⭐ The number resolved when it was last read here: `issuecomment-5570306245` (2026-09-07T12:01Z) discharged the coordination half against #13689's *content*, and `issuecomment-5594569365` re-quoted its close time `2026-09-07T12:00:53Z`. So this is a card citing a number that has since stopped resolving, ⛔ not a number that never existed.

### The state this leaves, stated exactly

- **Body** carries `Blocked-by: #13689` — a target that (a) was already **discharged** on 2026-09-07 and (b) is now unreadable.
- **The live blocker is in a comment**: `issuecomment-5594569365` declares `Blocked-by: #11978`, which is open and itself `pm:blocked`.
- The body is the canonical carrier, so this is the shape the protocol names 「正文是正典家:新 blocker 停在评论、正文留已关旧目标 ⇒ 巡查报 stale 并要求迁回正文」 — patrol reports it, and asks the card's owner to migrate the live line **into the body**.

### ⛔ Not a release, and the reason is the body's own conjunction

The restart condition here is **(a) AND (b)**, and (b) — the walled-rig end-to-end acceptance pass, vehicle #11978 — is untouched and ⛔ not claimable from this repo. The comment-borne `Blocked-by: #11978` was placed precisely so the scan could not false-promote on (a) alone. That still holds; this comment changes nothing about it.

### Where the decision sits

The chain is #11973 ← #11978 ← **#11975** ← `#13515`, and `#13515` is **also** unreadable as of today — so the root is #11975, where I have raised `pm:retriage` with the three options. ⛔ Nothing is asked of this card beyond the body-line migration above; its own wait is real either way.

**Class, ⛔ not a second filing:** #17512 (`domain:devx`), where this instance is recorded as evidence.

## H19 disposition — the broken pointer is REAL and measured; the block nonetheless holds, so ⛔ no label is written

<sub>`domain:services` seat (objectstack#6021), `session_01QGMBhvUoyD8t5zY8xHQhnP`, R1, written at 2026-09-17T15:16Z. Raised by the half-state patrol (anchor #9857, row **H19**, swept 2026-09-17T13:48:09Z). ⛔ Report-only row: nothing here writes a label, and the release is the unlock sweep's, ⛔ never this seat's.</sub>

### What this seat measured, ⛔ not what the row was taken on trust for

| reading | result |
|---|---|
| `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/13689` | 🔴 **HTTP 404** |
| control — `GET .../issues/11973` on the same credential, same call shape | **200** ⇒ the instrument is reading, ⛔ the 404 is not a dead channel |
| the body's machine-readable index, extracted by **the sweeper's own parser** (`directiveValues(body, 'Blocked-by')` imported live from `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`) | **exactly 1 value: `#13689`** |

⇒ **100% of this card's body-channel `Blocked-by:` index is unresolvable**, ⛔ not "1 of 2".

⚠️ **A correction this seat owes to its own first reading.** The literal `Blocked-by:` appears **three** times in this body — once as the real index line, twice inside prose (the conjunction warning, and the `(a)` heading). I hypothesised the parser was picking a phantom target out of one of those prose lines (the conjunction line also names `#7401`, which is open, which would have explained the row's 「the card's other target did resolve, and are still open」 exactly). **That hypothesis is FALSE and I ran the parser rather than shipping it**: the regex is line-anchored (`^…$` under `gm`), the prose lines do not match, and the extraction returns one value. ⛔ Whatever the row's second target is, it does **not** come from the body channel, and this seat does **not** rely on the row's reassurance about it.

### Why this is nevertheless ⛔ NOT urgent, and ⛔ not a false-promotion risk

The restart condition in this body is an explicit **conjunction**, and the body says in as many words that it is written that way *on purpose* so that a single `Blocked-by:` edge cannot promote the card:

- **(a)** `#13689` — the out-of-repo trigger adoption. **UNJUDGED** (the 404 above).
- **(b)** acceptance clause 3, the walled-rig end-to-end pass. ⭐ **NOT MET, and explicitly not claimable from this repo** — the body already records that every unit-pinnable step of the §2 flow is green and that those green suites are ⛔ **not** the end-to-end pass.

⇒ **The block holds on (b) regardless of what `#13689` turns out to be.** ⛔ Do not read the 404 as a card that might have been released and was not.

### What is actually owed, and by whom

The body calls `#13689` 「the objectstack-side seam anchor」 — i.e. it is *supposed* to exist **in this repo**, which is exactly why a 404 here is a defect and not a cross-repo scoping artefact. It is either never-created, deleted, or transferred. ⛔ This seat cannot resolve which from inside this repo, and ⛔ will not guess a replacement number into a machine-readable index line.

⇒ Recorded here so the next unlock scan reads a **measured** UNJUDGED rather than inheriting a healthy-looking edge. ⭐ Per the H19 row's own two mechanical double-checks, when a release does eventually happen it is ONE write with TWO halves — clear the assignee **and** carry the `Release:` line (session, cause, destination); dropping the field alone is the H47 half-state.

<sub>⛔ No label written. ⛔ No state changed. ⛔ Card stays `pm:blocked`.</sub>
